I learned from others during Hurricane Harvey that there was some interesting fine print when it came to deferring mortgage payments. Most mortgage companies were offering a one or two month deferment for payments because of the natural disaster and, naturally, I decided to start the application process myself. Why not get a couple months off from the note?

While waiting for a response, I was hearing from others, through word of mouth and on FB, that there was fine print stating that after the one or two months passed, the entire balance of what should have been paid would be due. Most assumed that there would be a couple of payments added to the end of the payment schedule in the same way that other loans do but this was not the case for mortgages. Needless to say, since I wan't flooded and didn't need to actually get the deferment, I decided to stop the process when they finally called me.

So, if you find yourself out of work and this option is offered, unless absolutely necessary, avoid doing this at all costs. The best option is probably to just miss some payments and get caught up as soon as possible. They won't foreclose on you for one payment. Remember who own the banks and they want their money. Good luck.
